1.mascotDialogue: All the splitting's just bookkeeping, mate — the real sorting happens entirely in the merge step, comparing two already-sorted halves and interleaving 'em correctly.

2.mascotDialogue: Lines 9 and 10 are the merge's heart — compare the fronts of both halves, take the smaller, advance only that side. Lines 12 and 13 mop up whichever half's still got leftovers once the other runs dry.

3.mascotDialogue: This view shows no swaps at all — merge sort doesn't swap in place, she writes the smaller of the two fronts into a fresh spot, with every comparison.

4.mascotDialogue: Easy to reckon the merge's done the second the main comparison loop ends — but one side almost always finishes before the other, and forgetting to drain the leftovers loses real data, quiet as you like.
